newsitem.title: SWITZERLAND: Novartis posts 19 pct first half sales rise.
newsitem.headline: Novartis posts 19 pct first half sales rise.

text.p: Swiss life sciences group Novartis AG reported a 19 percent rise in first half sales to 16.6 billion Swiss francs ($2.7 billion) and said strong growth in its pharmaceuticals and seeds businesses drove the expansion.

The first half sales were seven percent higher on a local currency basis. Novartis, formed late last year through the merger of Ciba-Geigy and Sandoz, reported comparable 1996 first half sales of 13.9 billion.
Sales of pharmaceuticals, the group's largest business segment, totalled 6.928 billion francs, representing an increase of 23 percent in Swiss francs and 10 percent in local currencies.
Seeds sales were 23 and nine percent higher, respectively, at 1.029 billion francs.
Novartis also said the acquisition of Merck & Co Inc's crop protection business further strengthened its leadership in the market.
Novartis announced the purchase of the crop protection business in May in a deal valued at $910 million.
The group's overall agribusiness sales were 16 percent higher in Swiss francs, and up four percent in local currencies, at 5.285 billion.
Nutrition sales were up 19 percent and six percent, respectively, at 2.084 billion. -- Zurich Editorial +41 1 631 7430 ($ = 6.152 French Francs)
